```plato

    //==
    // # Motor operations
    //
    // Construction, the dual-quaternion product, inversion, normalization, and
    // application for the rigid-motion motors of `transforms.types.plato`.

    //==
    // Motors — rigid motions in dual-quaternion form. IReal carries the
    // rotation; Dual = 0.5 * t * IReal carries the translation t (all products
    // Hamilton). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dual_quaternion

    // The motor of a rigid pose.
    Motor3D(pose: Pose3D): Motor3D {
        var q = pose.Orientation;
        var t = Quaternion(pose.Position.X, pose.Position.Y, pose.Position.Z, 0.0);
        return (q, t * q * 0.5);
    }

    // The pose of a motor: rotation from the real part, translation
    // t = 2 * Dual * conjugate(IReal).
    Pose3D(m: Motor3D): Pose3D {
        var q = m.Real.Normalize;
        var t = m.Dual * 2.0 * q.Conjugate;
        return (Point3D(t.X, t.Y, t.Z), q);
    }

    // A pure rotation as a motor (zero translation).
    Motor3D(q: Quaternion): Motor3D
        => (q, Quaternion(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0));

    // A rotor's rotation as a motor.
    Motor3D(r: Rotor3D): Motor3D
        => r.Quaternion.Motor3D;

    // A pure translation as a motor (identity rotation).
    CreateTranslation(_: Motor3D, v: Vector3D): Motor3D
        => (Quaternion.Identity, Quaternion(v.X * 0.5, v.Y * 0.5, v.Z * 0.5, 0.0));

    // The dual-quaternion product: like the quaternion Hamilton product,
    // a.Multiply(b) is the motion b followed by a. Use Compose for
    // first-then-second ordering.
    Multiply(a: Motor3D, b: Motor3D): Motor3D
        => (a.Real * b.Real, a.Real * b.Dual + a.Dual * b.Real);

    // The motor that applies `first`, then `second`.
    Compose(first: Motor3D, second: Motor3D): Motor3D
        => second * first;

    // The motor that undoes this one (the dual-quaternion conjugate; an
    // inverse for unit motors).
    Inverse(m: Motor3D): Motor3D
        => (m.Real.Conjugate, m.Dual.Conjugate);

    // Rescale so the real part has unit magnitude, restoring the motor
    // invariant after repeated products. Precondition: the real part is not
    // zero.
    Normalize(m: Motor3D): Motor3D {
        var scale = 1.0 / m.Real.Length;
        return (m.Real * scale, m.Dual * scale);
    }

    // Apply the motor's rigid motion to a point.
    Transform(p: Point3D, m: Motor3D): Point3D
        => p.Transform(m.Pose3D);

    // Alias for Transform with transform-on-left (* operator): m * p.
    Multiply(m: Motor3D, p: Point3D): Point3D
        => Transform(p, m);

    // Rotate a displacement by the motor's rotation (translation does not act
    // on vectors).
    Transform(v: Vector3D, m: Motor3D): Vector3D
        => v.Transform(m.Real);

    // Alias for Transform with transform-on-left (* operator): m * v.
    Multiply(m: Motor3D, v: Vector3D): Vector3D
        => Transform(v, m);

    // The homogeneous matrix of the motor's rigid motion.
    Matrix4x4(m: Motor3D): Matrix4x4
        => m.Pose3D.Matrix4x4;

    //==
    // # Point support
    //
    // The IDifference obligations of Point2D/Point3D, point interpolation, and the
    // explicit point <-> vector converters that every other transform library builds
    // on. Kept separate from the representations because nothing here depends on a
    // transform type.

    //==
    // Point support — the IOriginBased conversions of Point2D/Point3D/PointN, and
    // the explicit point <-> vector converters spelled in the direction callers
    // read them.
    //
    // NOTHING else is written here. Add, Between, Subtract (both spellings) and
    // Lerp are all derived from Offset and FromOffset via algebra.library.plato.
    // The converters remain deliberately named
    // rather than implicit conversions: silently coercing between positions and
    // displacements would defeat the point of keeping them distinct types.

    // The point's displacement from the origin.
    Offset(p: Point2D): Vector2D
        => (p.X, p.Y);

    // The point at the given displacement from the origin.
    FromOffset(_: Point2D, v: Vector2D): Point2D
        => (v.X, v.Y);

    // The point's displacement from the origin.
    Offset(p: Point3D): Vector3D
        => (p.X, p.Y, p.Z);

    // The point at the given displacement from the origin.
    FromOffset(_: Point3D, v: Vector3D): Point3D
        => (v.X, v.Y, v.Z);

    // The point's displacement from the origin. Arity is carried by the
    // component array, so no separate arity argument is needed.
    // Written as an explicit construction, not a parenthesized value: the single field is an
    // Array, and a C# backend cannot declare the implicit conversion for an interface-typed
    // field (CS0552), so the structural form has nothing to convert through.
    Offset(p: PointN): VectorN
        => VectorN(p.Components);

    // The point at the given displacement from the origin, of the delta's arity.
    FromOffset(_: PointN, v: VectorN): PointN
        => PointN(v.Components);

    //==
    // The named point <-> vector converters. These are the long-standing spelling
    // (curves-shapes.library.plato and the transform libraries call PositionVector);
    // they now delegate to the IOriginBased conversions rather than restating the
    // field copy, so there is one place where a point becomes a vector.
    // ToPoint reads in the opposite direction from FromOffset — it dispatches on
    // the VECTOR, which is what callers holding a vector want.

    // The point's displacement from the origin.
    PositionVector(p: Point2D): Vector2D
        => p.Offset;

    // The point's displacement from the origin.
    PositionVector(p: Point3D): Vector3D
        => p.Offset;

    // The point at the tip of the vector, placed from the origin.
    ToPoint(v: Vector2D): Point2D
        => (v.X, v.Y);

    // The point at the tip of the vector, placed from the origin.
    ToPoint(v: Vector3D): Point3D
        => (v.X, v.Y, v.Z);
```
